tool_summary: Changes file group ownership. Lower risk than chown/chmod since group membership alone rarely grants privileged access by itself, but -R applies the change across an entire directory tree at once.
platform_notes: Core syntax (-R, -h) is consistent between GNU and BSD chgrp.

rules.description: Recursively applies a group ownership change across an entire directory tree at once. Lower ceiling than chmod/chown recursion since group membership alone rarely grants privileged access by itself, but recursion is still worth attention: it is inherently harder to scope correctly, and neither commandant nor chgrp itself records the prior group to allow a clean undo. Combined with -L/-H (dereference symlinks), can also affect files outside the target directory if symlinks point elsewhere.
rules.reversible_note: Neither chgrp nor commandant records the prior group of affected files, so a recursive change cannot be cleanly undone without separately-recorded state.
